title: DevLoop integration eval cases - codegen + refactor
summary: Working set of integration-style evaluation cases and prompt recipes for onboarding code-generation/refactor model variants. Focused on compiling outputs, verifying unit test correctness, enforcing style constraints, and surfacing regression signal for CI gating.
body:
Purpose:
This doc collects candidate evaluation scenarios for the DevLoop onboarding pipeline. The goal is to create lightweight, reproducible end-to-end cases that exercise model outputs beyond lint-level checks: compile, run unit tests, and validate style/contract requirements. These are intended to plug into the onboarding CI harness and to be used by SEs when triaging model regressions.

Scope and constraints:
- Language focus: Python (3.10) and a small subset of TypeScript (Node 18) to start.
- Types of tasks: new code generation (function/class), automated refactor (rename/extract/inline), and repair (make tests pass).
- Evaluation stages: token-level scoring (baseline), compile/run, unit-test pass rates, behavioral equivalence checks, and style constraints (black/ruff or prettier/eslint).
- Time budget: each case must complete in < 30s on CI-worker (with cached deps) to avoid long onboarding blocks.

High-level case categories (each case below includes prompt template, example input, success criteria, flakiness notes):

1) Minimal compile & run (smoke)
- Intent: ensure generated code can be executed without syntax/runtime import errors.
- Prompt recipe: explicit system message requesting a single file or module; requests only code block output; no extra commentary. Ask for minimal dependencies and include a run snippet (if applicable).
- Example: generate a small class implementing a fixed interface (e.g., Stack with push/pop/peek). Provide simple usage snippet to run.
- Success: python -m py_compile returns 0 and the usage snippet returns expected value.
- Failure modes: stray commentary in output, missing imports, wrong function signatures.

2) Unit-test-driven repair
- Intent: Model reads failing unit tests and returns a patch/modified file to make tests pass.
- Prompt recipe: include failing test file and the current implementation; ask for a patch (unified diff) that fixes tests. Request only code in patch without analysis.
- Example: a small math utilities module with an off-by-one bug in prime counting; tests exercise edge cases.
- Success: applying patch and running pytest yields all tests green.
- Flakiness: sometimes model returns multiple plausible fixes; use determinism and top-k filtering in the harness to retry limited times.

3) Refactor with contract preservation
- Intent: refactor to meet a style/structure constraint while preserving external behavior.
- Prompt recipe: provide original implementation and a small black-box test harness that asserts public API. Ask model to extract a helper function and rename internal variables, preserving public function signatures. Include allowed style constraints (max line length, variable naming).
- Example: split a 200-line helper into two smaller functions.
- Success: tests pass and a static behavioral check (function outputs for N random inputs) matches within tolerance.
- Notes: measure metrics for behavior drift (diffs in outputs).

4) Compile + type-check for TS snippets
- Intent: ensure generated TypeScript code type-checks with tsconfig and builds.
- Prompt recipe: ask model for TS module implementing a typed interface; require export default. Include tsconfig minimal.
- Success: tsc --noEmit passes and basic node test runs.

5) Style constraint enforcement
- Intent: force adherence to style rules (Black + ruff or Prettier + eslint).
- Prompt recipe: explicitly require formatting and list the rules to check. Provide a pre-commit config or linter config used by the repo.
- Success: linter exit code success and diffs minimal relative to repo formatting.

Metrics and regression signals:
- Primary pass metrics: compile_success_rate, unit_test_pass_rate, style_compliance_rate.
- Secondary metrics: median_tokens, time_to_first_token, deterministic_variance (run-to-run pass delta), and human-review flags (when model suggests non-deterministic runtime behavior).
- Alert rules for CI: any drop > 5 percentage points in unit_test_pass_rate for the onboarding model across a fixed reference set triggers an auto-block and creates MLONB ticket.

Prompt templates (short canonical forms to seed prompt bank)
- Generation template (Python class):
  "You are an assistant that outputs a single Python file implementing the requested API. Provide only the code block starting with ```python and ending with ``` with no extra commentary. The file must be compatible with Python 3.10 and use no external dependencies beyond the standard library. Implement: {spec}. Include a short `if __name__ == "__main__"` example that prints a deterministic output for quick smoke tests."

- Repair template (patch):
  "You are given a failing pytest suite and one source file. Produce a unified diff patch (git format) that, when applied, makes the tests pass. Output only the patch. If more context is needed, request only the missing test name or a single failing stack trace line. Do not include commentary."

- Refactor template (preserve behavior):
  "Refactor the provided module to extract helper functions and reduce cyclomatic complexity below {target_cc}. Keep public API signatures unchanged. Provide the refactored file only in a single code block."

CI harness integration notes:
- Each case has a small runner in devloop-evals repo that:
  1) calls model with deterministic temp/seeds;
  2) extracts code blocks, strips extraneous text;
  3) applies patch or writes file;
  4) runs static checks (formatters/linters), compilers/type-checkers, pytest/mocha;
  5) records exit codes and artifacts to S3 for triage.
- Use container snapshotting to ensure repeatable dependency installs. Cache pip/NPX layers.
- Keep sandboxing strict: timeouts for tests (5s per unit test) and whole-case timeouts (30s).

Known failure patterns and mitigations:
- Extra natural language: model returns explanatory text around code. Mitigation: prompt stricter "ONLY code block" and post-parse filter to ignore leading text.
- Non-deterministic randomness in generated tests or examples. Mitigation: seed RNGs when running examples and require determinism in prompts.
- Over-reliance on external libs: model imports libs not in allowed list. Mitigation: enforce dependency whitelist and fail case if disallowed imports detected.
- Partial patches / incomplete diffs: fall back to file-level replacement prompts where diff fails.

Example case manifest (compact):
- case_id: dl-001, name: stack-impl-smoke, lang: python, stage: compile, prompt_template: generation template, timeout: 20s
- case_id: dl-042, name: primes-repair, lang: python, stage: unit-test, prompt_template: repair template, timeout: 30s
- case_id: dl-087, name: rename-extract, lang: python, stage: refactor, prompt_template: refactor template, timeout: 30s

Tagging and triage workflow:
- Every failing run auto-opens a triage item in Linear with metadata: case_id, model_version, prompt_seed, stdout/stderr, linter diff. Attach failing code artifact. Assign to oncall applied-ml rotation.
- For borderline failures (style only or flaky passes), annotate with severity low and monitor for 3 consecutive failures before blocking rollout.

Next steps and open questions:
- Expand corpus to include small Flask/FastAPI handlers and simple React components for TS path.
- Add behavioral equivalence harness (fuzzy-match outputs across random inputs) for numerical tolerances.
- Decide on long-term storage scheme for artifacts (S3 prefix naming and retention policy).
- Define automated rollback policy for Dedicated/Hosted serving if a model causes client-facing regressions (requires product + SRE input).

Appendix: quick checklist for creating new cases
1) Draft small repo snippet (< 150 LOC total).
2) Create a tight test harness with 4–8 unit tests, deterministic seeds.
3) Write prompt and sanitize to remove ambiguous language.
4) Validate locally with current onboarding model and capture baseline metrics.
5) Add case manifest entry and CI runner.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working collection; many cases are intentionally minimal to run fast. Feedback wanted on acceptable timeout budget on CI and whether TypeScript set should use Babel or TS-only compile checks.
- If you are triaging a flaky case, include the model invocation payload and the parsed code artifact in the Linear ticket so we can reproduce easily.

---
End of working doc.
